D18 — 2026-10-04
chose: 2.6 supersede-target integrity, in three parts. (1) Two-key hold. A decision can name a target its own words barely match (TF-IDF cosine under 0.16) while an in-force decision it could retire matches at least 2.5 times as much and at least 0.16. Or it can name a target that is already replaced or retired. Then the writer files it with the link held: supersedes moves to supersedes_held, link_candidates holds the named target first, then up to 2 better matches (or its replacement). The target stays in force. The write result, the digest and Stop ask for `sofar supersedes`. SOFAR_LINK_HOLD=off is the ablation arm. (2) decisions.md prints each entry's handle with a check suffix, D17·k3fz (4 Crockford base32 chars of sha256 of the event id). Every write path accepts D17·k3fz. When a merge moved the ordinal, it resolves by the suffix; it refuses a suffix that names nothing. The digest keeps bare [D<n>]. (3) Write results echo what a supersession retired, or that it retired nothing.
over: The survey's threshold as written: cosine under 0.12 with its own tokenizer, which with the engine's stemming tokenizer holds only 1 of the 2 known-wrong links. Refusing low-relatedness links: a refusal costs a resend, and a flagged link may be right. Suffixed handles in the digest too: 5 more chars on every handle line of a budgeted block at every session start, mirrored in Rust, for merges the hold already catches.
because: I replayed the shipped hold over round 3's 51 links, each against its pre-write fold. It holds 3 links.
